description: The Sweden Electricity Cost Calculator computes wholesale and distribution-network costs for user-supplied electricity load profiles. Gabriella Grenander at VTI publishes Python code with hourly spot-price inputs for Sweden’s four bidding areas in 2019–2024, network-tariff tables and JSON tariff rules. The README documents either a 24-hour template or 8,760-hour input, study-area mappings, customer classes and a CSV cost breakdown. Network concession shapefiles help select reporting entities but are not read directly by the calculator. The linked Zenodo v1.0 release is freely available under CC BY 4.0. GitHub retains an unfilled licence placeholder, so the licence assertion applies to the archive. The method excludes 29 February and handles local daylight-saving transitions; users must check that this convention matches their load data. Its tariffs and prices are historical inputs, not current quotations. No calculation was executed. A reviewer-assessed application is evaluating the distribution charges associated with load or storage schedules generated in model-pypsa; no direct interface is established.
